name: XL4015 adjustable 5 A buck module with voltmeter
description: XL4015 adjustable buck board with a built-in voltmeter and screw terminals, 1.25–32 V out at up to 4 A, for higher-current hobby rails.

variants.note: ProtoSupplies SKU; the same board is sold by many vendors

kicad.footprintNote: Ready-made module: wire it up with a connector or header

notes: Store rates it 4.5–38 V in / 1.25–35 V out; the XL4015 chip is rated 8–36 V in, 32 V out.
4 A continuous, 4.5 A max; fit the supplied heatsink above about 3 A.
Input has a reverse-polarity diode; the display draws extra current.

terminals.name: IN+
terminals.note: Screw terminal on the left end (display facing you), upper position. 4.5-38 V per the vendor page. Input has a reverse-polarity protection diode.

terminals.name: IN-
terminals.note: Screw terminal, left end, lower position. Ground.

terminals.name: OUT+
terminals.note: Screw terminal on the right end, upper position. Adjustable output, 1.25-35 V (derated to 35 V because of the 35 V output capacitor).

terminals.name: OUT-
terminals.note: Screw terminal, right end, lower position. Ground.

adjust.direction: clockwise raises Vout; counter-clockwise lowers Vout

notes: Screw terminals: input on the left, output on the right, when the LED display faces you.
The input has a reverse-polarity protection diode.
The output can be set no higher than about VIN - 1.5 V (e.g. about 10.5 V from 12 V in). The load condition is not stated.

Rated 4 A continuous and 4.5 A short-term, 75 W maximum. The vendor derates it from the 5 A sellers often claim. About 3 A is comfortable; above 4 A it runs hot. Keep the IC below about 80 °C for long-term µse.
A sudden excessive load can kill the XL4015 before thermal or current limiting reacts. Increase the load gradually.
Comes with an adhesive heatsink. It sticks to the IC's plastic body, so it helps only a little.
The built-in voltmeter (±0.1 V) runs from an LM317. Near the thermal limit, especially at high VIN, it can shut down and the display goes blank while the converter keeps working.
The left button turns the display on or off. The right button switches it between Vin and Vout, shown by the IN/OUT LEDs. A green LED lights when power is applied.
Output ripple and noise are typically 50-200 mV peak-to-peak. Switching frequency is 180 kHz (190 kHz measured).
Four corner mounting holes, with standoffs included.
Wire the input and output before applying power. Components get hot under heavy load.
